message.reasoning:
We need to fix compilation errors.

Issues:

- Mockito imports missing. Probably test environment doesn't have Mockito. We can remove Mockito usage. The test uses @Mock fields for JsonSchema, ValidatorTypeCode, ValidationContext. We can replace them with simple stub implementations or nulls.

Simplify: remove Mockito imports and annotations, just create dummy objects (maybe use null or simple mock objects). Since BaseJsonValidator constructor expects JsonSchema, ValidatorTypeCode, ValidationContext. We can pass null for these, as they are not used in getSchemaNode tests. So we can remove @Mock fields and just define them as null.

Also duplicate imports and redundant code in setup (mapper reinitialized). Clean up.

Another error: TestValidator extends BaseJsonValidator but BaseJsonValidator has abstract method validate with signature validate(ExecutionContext, JsonNode, JsonNode, String) maybe? The error says abstract method validate(ExecutionContext,JsonNode,JsonNode,String) in JsonValidator. Actually BaseJsonValidator implements JsonValidator which defines validate(ExecutionContext, JsonNode, JsonNode, String). Our TestValidator overrides validate(ExecutionContext, JsonNode) only. Need to override the correct method signature.

We can implement the method with full signature returning empty set.

Let's inspect BaseJsonValidator signature: Not given, but likely has method:

public Set<ValidationMessage> validate(ExecutionContext executionContext, JsonNode node, JsonNode rootNode, String at)

But test only needs validator to be constructed; validation not used. So we can implement that method.

Thus modify TestValidator:

@Override
public Set<ValidationMessage> validate(ExecutionContext executionContext, JsonNode node, JsonNode rootNode, String at) {
    return Collections.emptySet();
}

Also need to import ExecutionContext and ValidationMessage maybe. We'll import com.networknt.schema.ExecutionContext; com.networknt.schema.ValidationMessage.

Now remove Mockito imports and annotations.

Simplify class fields: private JsonSchema mockParentSchema; etc., but we can just set them to null in setup.

Or we can create simple stub classes implementing interfaces? JsonSchema is a class, not interface. We can instantiate a real JsonSchema? Might be complex. Use null.

Thus fields can be just JsonSchema parentSchema = null; etc.

But they are used only in constructor; null is fine.

Thus remove @Mock annotations.

Now adjust imports: remove org.mockito.* imports.

Also duplicate import of MockitoExtension; remove.

Now compile.

Potential other errors: BaseJsonValidator_getSchemaNode_Test class uses getSchemaPath method; BaseJsonValidator likely has getSchemaPath method returning string; fine.

Now need to ensure imports for Set, Collections, etc.

Now produce corrected code.
